questions.q: In SQL terms, what does 'reconciliation' generally mean?
options: Deleting all unmatched records
Converting text columns into numeric columns
Confirming that two numbers which should agree actually do, and identifying where they diverge
Running EXPLAIN PLAN on a query
questions.explain: Reconciliation compares two sides of the same economic event (e.g., invoice amount and amount paid) to confirm they agree, flagging exceptions when they don't.

questions.q: Why does the invoice-vs-paid reconciliation query use LEFT OUTER JOIN rather than INNER JOIN?
options: LEFT OUTER JOIN is always faster
INNER JOIN cannot be used with GROUP BY
There's no real reason — INNER JOIN would work identically
So invoices with zero payments still appear in the result, rather than disappearing entirely
questions.explain: An unpaid invoice has no matching row in ap_invoice_payments_all; INNER JOIN would drop it, but the reconciliation needs it to appear with total_paid = 0.

questions.q: Why is NVL needed around SUM(ip.amount) before subtracting it from invoice_amount?
options: Without it, an unpaid invoice's SUM could be NULL, and invoice_amount minus NULL would itself be NULL, breaking the HAVING comparison
NVL makes the query run faster
NVL is required syntax for every SUM in Oracle
NVL converts the amount into a different currency
questions.explain: SUM over a LEFT JOIN with no matching rows returns NULL, and NULL arithmetic propagates NULL — NVL substitutes 0 to keep the subtraction meaningful.

questions.q: Why does the reconciliation query filter with `HAVING difference <> 0` rather than returning every invoice?
options: To intentionally hide problem invoices from the report
Because a reconciliation report should surface only the exceptions — fully paid invoices (difference = 0) aren't useful to show
HAVING <> 0 is required syntax with no real effect
Because WHERE cannot be used with aggregated differences
questions.explain: The point of a reconciliation report is to find discrepancies, so filtering out zero-difference (fully reconciled) rows focuses the report on real exceptions.

questions.q: What does a nonzero `unapplied_amount` on a cash receipt indicate?
options: The receipt was recorded in the wrong currency
The customer has not yet paid at all
The receipt amount was entered twice
Money was received but has not yet been matched to any invoice
questions.explain: Unapplied cash means a receipt exists but some or all of its amount hasn't been applied to a specific transaction yet, leaving the customer's AR balance inaccurate.
